quotes.text: SharePoint was built for content and collaboration. Documents, pages, conversations, basic lists. It's excellent at that. But a Power App is a data application. It needs a data platform that speaks relationships, delegation, and server-side execution.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Names the architectural mismatch at the core of the episode.

quotes.text: When Power Apps can't delegate a query, it pulls data to the client and evaluates locally. That's fast in demos and catastrophic at scale.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains delegation failure in two plain sentences.

quotes.text: Security filtering is still filtering. If it's not efficient, your app pays the tax every tap.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable point on why item-level permissions slow apps down.

quotes.text: Delegation warnings predict wrong results. Load time patterns reveal where you force the client to do server work. Record counts expose the difference between can store and can query.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives three measurable signals of an architectural mismatch.

quotes.text: Choose Dataverse when any of the following are true. Your list will exceed 100,000 items. Users need compound filters or multicolumn search. You have more than one or two lookups per record.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concrete decision thresholds for moving from SharePoint lists to Dataverse.

chapters.title: SharePoint lists are not a database
Cost reality and total cost of ownership

takeaways: SharePoint lists are built for content and collaboration, so Power Apps on top of them hit delegation limits, the 5,000-item list view threshold and slow item-level security.
Dataverse runs filters, joins, aggregations and row- and field-level security on the server, so apps stay correct and fast as data grows.
Move to Dataverse when lists exceed about 100,000 items, need compound filters, multiple lookups, offline or granular auditing, or when blue delegation banners appear in core screens.
hook: Power Apps built on SharePoint lists often stall at 2,000 records, show blue delegation warnings and slow down as permissions grow. This episode gives makers and IT leaders the architectural reasons, measurable red flags, cost arguments and a migration path for deciding when an app belongs on Dataverse.
